6. It appears from the lower Court records (LCR) that on 2-6-2022 the Tribunal heard the arguments of the learned Advocates of both sides and relying on the case reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 236 = 38 DLR (AD) 275 (para 13) passed an order for recounting of the ballot papers holding that the petitioner of the election case (present respondent No. 2) succeeded by adducing evidence in preparing the foundation for recounting. The Tribunal observed, 

 15. In Nurul Islam Talukdar vs Munsif of the 4th Court at Sadar Chittagang acting as Election Tribunal and 10 others, 28 DLR 375, it was held: 

 16. In Nowsher Ali Molla vs Election Tribunal and Sadar Munsif, Faridpur and another, 33 DLR 344 this Division held that the Election Tribunal acted illegally in declaring the petitioner's election as void and illegal on the basis of the recounting of votes without considering the evidence adduced by the parties. The case was remanded back to the Tribunal to decide on the basis of existing evidence and in accordance with law and to receive further evidence, if considered necessary. 

 17. In Afzal Khan vs The Election Tribunal and Munsif 3rd Court, Comilla and another, 1980 BSCR 69 = 32 DLR (AD) 186, the Appellate Division held as correct the following views of the High Court Division— 

 20. The above-quoted dicta given in 1980 BSCR 69 = 32 DLR (AD) 186 as well the ratio laid down in 31 DLR (AD) 296, 27 DLR 594, 28 DLR 375 and 33 DLR 344 were discussed and considered by a single Bench of this Division in Moulana Abdul Hague vs Faziul Huq and others, 38 DLR 401 wherein the Rule was made absolute and the case was sent back on remand to the Tribunal holding: 

 21. In Syed A Jalil vs Mahbub Alam (Babul) and others, 46 DLR (AD) 96, it was held: 

 22. In Md Shajahan vs Md Sadeq and another, 1986 BLD (AD) 236 = 38 DLR (AD) 275 (referred by the Tribunal in support of passing the order of recounting), the Apex Court referred to the case reported in 28 DLR 375 (supra) and held: 

 25. In the instant case, the judgments passed by the Tribunal and the Appeal Tribunal are totally silent as to the facts, circumstances and evidence on record which persuaded them to pass the order of recounting. Before passing the final judgment on 14-6-2022 Tribunal, vide an earlier order dated 2-6-2022 very briefly discussed the evidence on record which, in our view, does not constitute "sufficient foundation". The Tribunal relied on the case reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 236 = 38 DLR (AD) 275 in passing the order of recounting. We are afraid the Tribunal failed to appreciate the true spirit of the reported case and misdirected itself in applying the said case as a ground for passing the recounting order. 

 27. In Amizuddin Ahmed vs Election Tribunal, Narayanganj and others, 27 DLR 594, the Tribunal appointed the Pleader Commissioner to reopen the ballot boxes, recount the ballot papers, determine the validity of those and to submit his report to that effect. It was held that determination of the validity of the ballot papers is a mixed question of law and fact and such a question cannot be delegated to the Pleader Commissioner for determination. It was further held that acceptance of the report means the end of the whole matter inasmuch as the Tribunal is left only with the formality of delivering the judgment. 

 28. Before recounting the ballot papers, the Tribunal must be satisfied that the gunny bags containing the election materials have not been tampered with. Examination of the Presiding Officer is indispensably necessary if the Tribunal finds tampered ballot papers (28 DLR 375) or the Tribunal should advert to the other evidence and take the decision on consideration of other relevant facts (33 DLR 344). The Tribunal must see whether the ballot boxes were kept in proper custody from the time of its dispatch by the Presiding Officer till its final destination and whether the sealed bags containing the ballot packets as well as the sealed ballot packets are intact. In that connection evidence of competent witness including the Presiding Officer concerned should be recorded [46 DLR (AD) 96].
